thread:
maria: Heads-up — running a new on-call shadowing plan for tonight to cover the late PST window and to onboard 2 new shadows. I'm primary 23:00-07:00 PST. There is a small gap we identified between 03:00-04:00 PST where scheduled infra maintenance could reduce available capacity. Looking for volunteers to shadow, and one backup to be secondary in case pages escalate.

alex: I can do shadowing for the first half (23:00-02:00). Happy to pair on handoff procedures. :+1:

sam: I can pick up 02:00-05:00 and act as secondary if needed. Are we keeping the same ack/escalation flow?

maria: Yes — follow the standard paging flow. Quick refresher in case anyone new: 1) Acknowledge page within 2 minutes using `/ack` in the pager or Opsgenie app, 2) Triage using runbook pointers, 3) If P1 and you can't mitigate within 15m, escalate to secondary and open an incident channel.

jess: Who are the new shadows? I can do a 30m pre-shift walkthrough so they know the essentials (how to read the dashboards, where the runbooks are, common mitigation steps).

maria: New shadows are @kevin and @rachel (Rachel is remote, starting her first shadow). Plan: 30m handoff/overview at 22:30 PST, then in-shift shadowing (kevin pairs with alex first, rachel pairs with sam).

oncall-bot: INCIDENT BOT: NOTE: scheduled infra maintenance in us-west region at 03:00-03:40 UTC — may cause transient model hot-reloads and increased 5xx. See maintenance ticket: https://redwood-internal/incidents/MT-2389

alex: Thanks bot. If we see cache thrash or higher p99, do we failover to warm pool or switch routing policy? Which runbook section covers that?

maria: Runbook pointers: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/oncall-handoff (handbook) and https://redwood-internal/runbooks/production-fallbacks (failover steps). Quick notes pasted below for tonight's shadowing: \n```
- If 5xx rate >5% and sustained 3m: check serving-runtime logs: `kubectl logs -l app=serving -n redwood-prod --since=5m`
- Check gateway errors: `curl -sS http://gateway.health/metrics | jq '.requests_errors'`
- If KV cache eviction high and latency spikes: enable routed-cache fallback: `rctl set-routing --policy warm-pool`
- For model OOMs: scale down batch size via runtime flag `--max-batch-size 8` and alert infra.
```

sam: Appreciate the snippet — can we add the exact Opsgenie escalation list and phone numbers in the handoff doc? New folks will want it obvious.

maria: Will add. Also adding a quick checklist for shadows: 
- join #eng-oncall 10m before shift
- confirm you can access runbooks + logs (ask for VPN if needed)
- watch one page with primary, then take a page while primary observes (30-60m)
- run through a simulated mitigation (15m)

kevin: I'm set on VPN and runbook access. One question: if we get a P1 with active customer impact, do shadows ever respond directly or must primary always take the lead?

jess: Shadows can triage and run read-only commands (logs, dashboards), but any action that changes routing or restarts nodes should be done by primary unless primary authorizes. That's our safety policy.

maria: Correct. Shadows will practice safe triage: gather facts, reproduce if possible, propose mitigation steps, then primary approves action. We want the shadow to be able to acknowledge and gather context quickly.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT BOT: PAGER NOTE — If you mark an alert `ack` the bot logs the ack time into the incident timeline. Use `/ack PAGER_ID` or acknowledge in Opsgenie.

alex: For the handoff tonight I'll run through: dashboard locations (console > routing > per-model p99), common logs, how to interpret `kv_cache_miss_rate`, and the fallback toggles. Any objections to a short pre-shift doc I can paste into the channel at 22:20?

maria: No objections — paste it. Also include the customer-impact assessment template: \n```
Customer Impact Assessment quick template:\n- Affected surface: hosted api / dedicated / private
- Percentage affected: estimate requests/users
- Severity: P1 (customer-facing outage), P2 (degraded), P3 (minor)
- Mitigation in place: e.g., routing fallback, autoscale bump
- ETA to restore: ballpark in minutes
- Owner: primary oncall
```

sam: One more ops note: if you need to bring infra oncall (pager id infra-oncall), tag `@infra-oncall` in the incident channel and mention `investigate:server` in Opsgenie. That gets them in fast.

kevin: Got it. Do we have a documented way to hand off mid-shift if primary needs to step away?

maria: Yes — use the handoff template in the runbook (section 'mid-shift handoff'). Quick version: 1) create a short thread in #eng-oncall with `handoff: from X to Y`, 2) list active alerts and top 3 ongoing mitigations, 3) confirm Y acked and observed a page (Y must deliberately ack to accept responsibility). Also add estimated time until X returns.

jess: I'll lead the 22:30 walkthrough. If anyone can't make the walkthrough, ping me 10m before and we'll reschedule.

alex: I'll paste the mini-doc at 22:20 and be on the call at 22:30.

maria: Thanks all. Final note for shadows: practice humility, ask lots of questions, and log everything in the incident timeline. We'll do a quick retro tomorrow morning if anything interesting happens. :coffee:

kevin: Thanks — excited to shadow and learn the runbooks.

oncall-bot: SYSTEM: Reminder — new shadow onboarding checklist assigned to @kevin and @rachel. Task links: https://redwood-internal/tasks/SHADOW-115

maria: Closing thread for coordination. If anything changes (maintenance window shifts, extra pages), update here and we'll reassign.
